terms.gloss: a set form, rule; a formula
evidence: Cic. Leg. 1.4 fin.: stipulātiōnum et jūdiciōrum formulās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a fixed form of words, above all in law, and a rule or pattern; Morgan–Owens gives it, after Gauss and nineteenth-century books of medicine, for a mathematical or chemical formula. Diminutive of forma.

phrases.latin: sunt jūra, sunt formulae dē omnibus rēbus cōnstitūtae
phrases.english: there are laws, there are formulas laid down for every case

formula-o.html: Lewis & Short marks neither forma nor formula, and the lexicon writes forma unmarked (ideal). De Vaan 233, s.v. forma, reports Ernout–Meillet’s long o but explains it as a recent lengthening before -rC- (Leumann 1977: 114): a question for a ruling.

sources: Lewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: forma
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. formula (math.).
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), p. 233.
